description: Hand morphology: hand size, palm shape, finger length proportions (digit ratio 2D:4D), finger morphology, nail morphology, knuckle prominence. The 2D:4D digit ratio is the most-cited individual hand-anthropometry dimension; Manning's prenatal-androgen-exposure hypothesis remains debated but the ratio itself is a well-established measurement with population-level variation.

dimensions.scale_citation: Aligned with anthropometric descriptors of hand-length proportional to height (typical ratio ~10.4-11.0%).
dimensions.description: Hand length relative to body height, captured qualitatively.

dimensions.scale_citation: Aligned with descriptors used in chiromancy-adjacent hand-anthropometry literature.
dimensions.description: Shape of the palm in proportional terms.

values.definition: Palm length approximately equal to palm width.
Palm width approaches or exceeds length.

dimensions.scale_citation: Manning JT, Scutt D, Wilson J, Lewis-Jones DI (1998). The ratio of 2nd to 4th digit length: a predictor of sperm numbers and concentrations of testosterone, luteinizing hormone and oestrogen. Human Reproduction, 13(11): 3000-3004.
dimensions.description: Ratio of index-finger length (2D) to ring-finger length (4D). Sex-dimorphic on average (males ~0.95-0.98, females ~0.97-1.00) with substantial individual variation.

values.definition: 2D:4D ratio < ~0.95; ring finger clearly longer than index. More common in males.
2D:4D ratio ~0.95-1.00; subtle or no length difference.
2D:4D ratio > ~1.00; index finger clearly longer than ring. Less common; more common in females.

observability.notes: Best assessed when hand is open, palm-up or palm-down with extended fingers; finger curl confounds assessment.

dimensions.scale_citation: Aligned with hand-anthropometry descriptors used in glove-fitting and ergonomics literature.
dimensions.description: Overall thickness and shape of the fingers.

values.definition: Wider at the base, narrower at the tips.

dimensions.scale_citation: Aligned with surface-anatomy descriptors of metacarpophalangeal-joint visibility.
dimensions.description: Visibility of the metacarpophalangeal joints as surface landmarks.

values.definition: Knuckles barely visible; soft-tissue coverage smooth.
Clear knuckle landmarks even at rest.

dimensions.scale_citation: Aligned with descriptors used in dermatology and manicure literature.
dimensions.description: Native fingernail shape when not artificially shaped.

values.definition: Often artificial; native nails rarely take this shape.
Visible manicure or artificial nails; native shape not assessable.

dimensions.scale_citation: Aligned with frame-size literature; wrist circumference is the standard Frisancho frame-size proxy.
dimensions.description: Wrist circumference relative to body proportions. Different from but related to body-shape.json's frame_size_estimate.

references: Manning JT, Scutt D, Wilson J, Lewis-Jones DI (1998). The ratio of 2nd to 4th digit length: a predictor of sperm numbers and concentrations of testosterone, luteinizing hormone and oestrogen. Human Reproduction, 13(11): 3000-3004.
Frisancho AR (1984). New standards of weight and body composition by frame size and height. American Journal of Clinical Nutrition, 40(4): 808-819.
Greiner TM, Gordon CC (1990). Anthropometry and Mass Distribution for Human Analogues. US Army Natick Laboratories Technical Report.
